sections.content: A variable is a named box that stores a value. Instead of repeating a value everywhere, you store it once and reuse the name.
Variables can hold text (strings), whole numbers (integers), decimals (floats), and true/false values (booleans). Assigning a new value replaces the old one.
Key points: names should describe content (userAge, not x), most languages are case-sensitive, and you must declare or assign before use.
Summary: Variables — practice the example by changing values and predicting the output before running it.
